title: Ensure verification of signed commits for new changes before merging
description: Git commit authorship is self-asserted: anyone who can push can claim to be anyone. Verifying signatures at the server is what makes the audit trail mean something.
remediation: Bitbucket Data Center 8.13 and later bundle a "Verify Commit Signature" pre-receive hook: enable it at Repository settings -> Hooks, or at Project settings -> Hooks to cover every repository in the project, and make sure the signing keys of your committers are registered (GPG and SSH keys under Profile -> Manage account). "Verify Committer" is a different hook — it checks who pushed, not whether a commit is signed — and does not satisfy this control. On an older instance, install a signature-verification add-on from the Atlassian Marketplace and add its full hook key (plugin-key:module-key) to signatureHookKeys; a captured snapshot lists every hook's key under repositories[].hooks[].key.
fixSummary: Enable the "Verify Commit Signature" hook at Repository settings -> Hooks.
